🚀 Lunar Forge

Somos uma equipe apaixonada por tecnologia, programação, ciência e exploração espacial. Nosso objetivo é desenvolver um jogo educativo de missões espaciais para o NASA Space Apps Challenge. Buscamos pessoas com conhecimentos em Física, Astronomia, Matemática, Game Design ou desenvolvimento de jogos que queiram inovar e construir algo incrível conosco! 🌙
summary:
Icarus Program is an interactive browser-based space mission simulator that challenges players to design, build, and fly their own space missions.

Players can choose between climate satellite, Moon landing, Mars landing, and sandbox missions. They must manage limited budgets, rocket mass, fuel, power, scientific instruments, and communication capacity while making critical decisions throughout the mission.

Using the Ideal Rocket Equation, the simulator demonstrates how engineering trade-offs affect mission performance and survival. Players can work individually or collaborate in teams of up to four people, then review their mission results and try again.

Icarus Program transforms complex aerospace concepts into an engaging learning experience, making the challenges of space exploration accessible through interactive experimentation.
details:
Icarus Program is a browser-based educational space mission simulator designed to introduce players to the engineering challenges involved in planning and executing space missions.


Players begin by selecting a mission: a climate observation satellite, a two-person Moon landing, a four-person Mars landing, or a customizable sandbox mission. The experience supports individual play or collaborative gameplay for up to four participants sharing one computer.


During the hangar preparation phase, players must design their spacecraft within limited budget and mass constraints. They select rocket components, scientific instruments, orbital parameters, and launch vehicles.

Each player can take responsibility for a different mission role:


●Mission Lead: selects the orbit, launch vehicle, and launch strategy.
●Spacecraft: manages spacecraft components and configuration.
●Science: selects scientific instruments and balances their scientific value against power and data requirements.
●Communications: evaluates communication limitations and decisions involving data transmission.

Players can also manage every role individually.

The simulator presents important mission parameters, including budget, launch mass, thrust-to-weight ratio, delta-v, electrical power, and communication capacity.

Rocket delta-v is calculated using the Ideal Rocket Equation, demonstrating how propellant mass, structural mass, and engine performance influence the available velocity change. Additional mass reduces the available propellant margin, while mission orbits influence the required velocity budget.

Scientific instruments generate research value but also consume electrical power and produce data. Their effectiveness depends on the spacecraft's available resources and communication capacity.

After launch, the mission unfolds through a sequence of interactive events. Players must make decisions that affect fuel, spacecraft integrity, oxygen, scientific output, and mission time. Every decision involves trade-offs between safety, efficiency, and scientific objectives.

At the end of each mission, the simulator generates a performance report containing the mission score and decision timeline. Results are stored locally in the browser, allowing players to review previous attempts, compare strategies, and redesign their missions.

The project was developed using React 18 and Vite, with no backend server required. Mission progress is stored locally in the browser.

The development process was supported by Cursor, an AI coding assistant used to help draft code and on-screen text. The team subsequently tested, reviewed, and corrected the implementation. The demonstration narration was recorded by a team member.

Icarus Program aims to make aerospace engineering concepts more accessible by allowing students to experience the consequences of mission planning decisions through experimentation, collaboration, and interactive learning.
